text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Britain's new Labour government affirms its commitment to the security of Kuwait. Kuwait's Prime Minister and Crown Prince Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah on Tuesday received Britain's Minister of State Derek Fatchett.
- Coast Guard patrol foils alleged infiltration attempt by three Iraqi boats near Kuwaiti waters. The boats fled.

- Banning concerts violates the constitution, Information Minister Sheikh Saud Nasser al-Sabah told editors of local newspapers. Parliament last week rejected a bill to ban concerts and fashion shows.
- Gulf Arab and European businessmen started on Tuesday meetings in Riyadh to discuss boosting cooperation.
- Kuwait's Acting Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah says Kuwait will not deal with Israeli firms before an Arab-Israeli peace settlement is reached.
- Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan to head Kuwait's team at meetings next week in Qatar by the economic committee of Gulf Arab states.
- Sheikh Sabah says Kuwait would welcome any summit that would serve Arab causes.
- Kuwait's Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah to attend on Wednesday the graduation of new army officers.
- Kuwait will soon promote National Guard officers.
- About 1,200 people undergo treatment for post traumatic stress disorder following the 1990-91 Iraqi occupation of Kuwait, Health Ministry official says.
